pronunciation.approximation: Say "belobog" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Belobog".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "belobog" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Belobog" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Belobog
domains.subtitle: Light
domains.lead: Belobog is light, good, fortune. The name means "White god" and belongs to the slavic tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name
cards.desc: The restoration Belobog returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in slavic myth, cult, and cultural memory.

cards.name: Unicode Restoration
cards.desc: Preserved as a flagship temple despite the unregistrable plain-ASCII form.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.meaning: The restored form Belobog, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.

mythology.lead: The stories of Belobog place light, good, fortune at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Belobog appears in slavic tradition as light, good, fortune. The name's meaning, "White god", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Belobog in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Belobog remains a touchstone for understanding slavic religion, art, and identity.
scholarlySources: Ivanits, Linda J., Russian Folk Belief (1989).
Toporov, V. N., and O. N. Trubachev, Linguistic Analysis of Reconstructed Slavic Mythology.
